tasks.title: Author the wedge-safe stream-primitive first-light bench, its receipts bound, and the transport decision memo
tasks.goal: Author (never run — the dead-last checkpoint runs it) a wedge-safe first-light benchmark of the in-tree USB4 stream primitive, as transport-decision evidence for the morning. Deliverables: (1) bench/usb4stream-bench.py — one file serving both roles (coordinator role is the default; peer role via --role peer --dev PATH; the peer is launched by streaming this same file over the control wire: ssh worker with the script on stdin, never a copy). Non-negotiable mechanics, each existing because an open/close storm against a mismatched peer wedges router hop tables and already darkened rail 0 once: (a) NEVER hardcode a numbered device node and never write a digit directly after the word tbstream anywhere in the file — the numbering is asymmetric across the twins and the coordinator carries PEERLESS cable-B groups at the low indices, where a blocking open waits forever; resolve on EACH node as: the rail netdev carrying the 10.99.0.0/30 address, then readlink /sys/class/net/RAIL/device, then the parent xdomain, then the sibling service whose key attribute is stream, then the configfs group fn0's index attribute, then the device node /dev/tbstream suffixed with that index; require BOTH ends' fn0 configfs groups to exist before any open. (b) Exactly ONE open attempt per side, ever, blocking, under a 30 s alarm; any failure after that point: close whatever is open, kill the ssh child, write the receipt, exit — never reopen, never retry, never write configfs (read ring_size and throttling only). (c) Idempotence guard: if results/receipts/usb4stream.json already exists, exit 0 immediately WITHOUT touching any device — this is what makes harness retries storm-free by construction. (d) Skip preconditions, checked in this order BEFORE any device access, each producing receipt status pass with data.outcome 'skipped:REASON' and exit 0: (i) the pair serve is up — the API answers on the coordinator, or podman reports the serving container running on either node (check the worker over the control wire) — outcome 'skipped:serve-up-on-shared-cable': the stream device shares cable A with the serving rails and a wedge would take the campaign's headline deliverable down, so this bench runs ONLY on an idle cable; (ii) ping -c1 -W2 to the rail peer fails — outcome 'skipped:rail-peer-unreachable'; (iii) either end's fn0 configfs group is missing — outcome 'skipped:configfs-group-missing'. Record data.serve_up true or false in EVERY receipt including skips. (e) Fixed schedule, no adaptivity, no retries: 50 iterations of 4 KiB ping-pong warmup (discarded); RTT at 64, 4096, 16384, 65536 bytes times 500 iterations with p50 and p99 per size; the allreduce-shaped simultaneous exchange at 8192, 16384, 65536 bytes times 500 (both sides write N bytes then read N bytes — ring 1024 times 4 KiB frames buffers this safely); throughput 256 MiB each direction; under 90 s wall total, whole run under a global timeout. (f) The receipt at results/receipts/usb4stream.json: one JSON object, step 'usb4stream', status ALWAYS 'pass' — this bench is evidence-gathering, not a campaign claim, so a mid-run abort is typed as data.outcome 'aborted:PHASE:ERRNO' rather than a fail status that would redden every later gate run; data carries outcome, per-size rtt and exchange p50/p99 fields, throughput both directions, ring_size and throttling as read from configfs, resolved device paths on both ends, open_count (assert exactly 1 per side), serve_up, and loop 'python' for honesty about syscall-loop overhead. (2) scripts/receipts-verify.py: add a 'usb4stream' entry to the BOUNDS table — outcome 'ok' requires open_count 1 and all schedule fields present; 'skipped:' and 'aborted:' outcomes require their reason text and pass. (3) docs/USB4STREAM-TRANSPORT.md — the decision memo: why the collective-library net-plugin route is REJECTED for the latency goal (it sits under the library's proxy and protocol stack, HopID scarcity shared with the network paths forces a multiplexer over one or two long-lived streams, and comm teardown on every serve restart is exactly the open/close pattern the wedge hazard forbids; 3-5 attended days to a fragile prototype, 2-4 attended weeks to overnight-trustworthy); why the real path is a 2-4 attended-day port of the reference doorbell-plus-progress-thread allreduce (the 105 microsecond reference bar) from verbs onto the stream device's read and write, with the receive path run by the progress thread; the morning trigger criteria (banked exchange p50 at 8-16 KiB at or under about 40 microseconds AND the bench matrix showing allreduce-dominated decode); the note that after a healthy night the first real run happens attended in the morning AFTER the pair is torn down (the serve-up skip is deliberate); and a drafted-not-filed issue body for the port. (4) tests/test_usb4stream_bench.py: py-compile both edited python files, assert the no-hardcoded-device-node invariant (no digit after tbstream in the bench source), assert the idempotence guard and the serve-up skip are present, and exercise the receipts checker's three outcome branches with synthetic receipt dicts. Boundaries: touch only bench/usb4stream-bench.py, docs/USB4STREAM-TRANSPORT.md, scripts/receipts-verify.py, and tests/.
deliveredBehaviors: A single-open, skip-safe, retry-proof bench that can bank the first stream-primitive exchange numbers without being able to storm the hop tables, and that refuses to touch the device while the pair is serving on the same cable
The morning reads one memo that settles plugin-versus-port with trigger criteria instead of re-deliberating

Measure ROCm 10.0.0 viability on a separate image tag, off the critical path, after the bench
tasks.goal: Measure whether the ROCm 10.0.0 substrate is viable for this fork on this hardware, without touching the 7.14 lane that served the night. Context: a complete aligned gfx1151/cp312 wheel set exists at https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/ (verified 2026-08-30; wheels dated 2026-08-26; same upstream versions and the SAME triton git hash 4cff872c as the current pins, so the swap is a pure version-literal substitution) — but no upstream anywhere has run this engine on ROCm 10 on gfx1151, and two failure modes are unmeasured: whether ROCm 10's hipcc compiles the fork's HIP sources, and whether its HSA runtime binds to the in-tree KFD on this kernel. This lane answers both as DATA. Build a second image flashnext:rocm10 from the UNMODIFIED container/Containerfile using its existing build ARGs (ROCM_WHL, TORCH_PIN, TORCHVISION_PIN, TRITON_PIN, ROCM_DEVEL_PIN, DEVICE_PINS at container/Containerfile:48-65 — no recipe edit, so the banked container-recipe acceptance stays true): podman build --tag flashnext:rocm10 --file container/Containerfile --build-arg ROCM_WHL=https://stable.repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-next/ --build-arg 'TORCH_PIN=torch==2.13.0+rocm10.0.0' --build-arg 'TORCHVISION_PIN=torchvision==0.28.0+rocm10.0.0' --build-arg 'TRITON_PIN=triton==3.8.0+git4cff872c.rocm10.0.0' --build-arg 'ROCM_DEVEL_PIN=rocm-sdk-devel==10.0.0' --build-arg 'DEVICE_PINS=amd-torch-device-gfx1151==2.13.0+rocm10.0.0 amd-torchvision-device-gfx1151==0.28.0+rocm10.0.0 rocm-sdk-device-gfx1151==10.0.0' . (a prefetched wheel set may exist under ~/.cache/flashnext-wheels/rocm10/). Then, on the coordinator only, run a minimal GPU binding check in that image (--device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --ipc=host): torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName, a small fp16 and a small fp8-block matmul, and importing the engine package. Record the ROCm/HSA and KFD versions the runtime reports plus the running kernel release (a green probe on a 7.2.0 coordinator is strong but not conclusive for the pair; a red probe attributable to KFD must be re-checked on 7.2.2 before ROCm 10 is written off — say so in the notes field). Do not load the checkpoint, do not start a server, do not touch the worker. WRITE THE RECEIPT TO results/rocm10-probe.json — NOT under results/receipts/: scripts/receipts-verify.py fails the campaign gate on any fail-status receipt in that directory, and this lane exists to record an outcome, green or red, never to fail the campaign. The receipt carries {step:'rocm10-probe', status, ts, data:{build_ok, compile_seconds, torch, triton, rocm_sdk_core, gcn_arch, cuda_available, matmul_fp16_ok, matmul_fp8_block_ok, engine_import_ok, kernel_release, notes}} with status 'pass' whenever an outcome was recorded. Never remove or retag flashnext:dev; never edit container/, results/receipts/, or the worklist. If the night is running late this lane is the first thing the operator drops. Boundaries: touch only results/rocm10-probe.json.
deliveredBehaviors: By morning the ROCm 10 question is answered with a measured receipt on this exact hardware instead of a guess
The proven 7.14 image and the whole receipt contract are untouchable by construction
